findings.title: A valid basic.json can bypass the version guard
findings.claim: If basic.json has more than 4,096 bytes before its stored simVersion, basicVersion returns undefined. With the other two artifacts already at the current version, bless proceeds without the per-tick proof.
findings.why: A JSON file with leading whitespace remains valid. An in-memory probe with 4,096 leading spaces, stored version 36, and the other versions at 37 produced no detected stale version. The guard can then overwrite the older golden without proof.
findings.fix: Read and validate the structural simVersion from the complete basic.json. Treat an existing file whose version cannot be read as an error, and test the padded-file case.

findings.title: The retired baseline still has an overwrite command
findings.claim: The retained capture script can rewrite net1a-baseline.json, contrary to the decision that the historical oracle is never written.
findings.why: An explicit invocation overwrites the pinned baseline even though R-0 retires it to a read-only historical check.
findings.fix: Remove or disable the capture script's write path while leaving the pinned baseline untouched.

findings.title: The same-mode proof has no automated failure test
findings.claim: No test exercises verifyUnchanged or the same CLI branch, despite R-1 depending on their failure behavior.
findings.why: The shared comparison and exit path look correct by inspection, but a later change could make the R-1 proof report success on a changed tick without a test catching it.
findings.fix: Add a small test using a synthetic baseline and injected trace: change one tick hash and assert failure. Cover missing baseline and moved version in the same test group.
